title: Chapter 10 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of Flexbox concepts, container and item properties, and common layout patterns!

questions.question: To make a container a flex container, you set:
questions.explanation: `display: flex;` or `inline-flex` creates a flex container.

questions.question: Flex items are always the direct children of a flex container.
questions.explanation: Only direct children become flex items; grandchildren are not affected.

questions.question: Which property sets the direction of the main axis?
questions.explanation: `flex-direction` defines the main axis (row, column, etc.).

questions.question: What does `flex-wrap: wrap;` do?
options: Allows items to wrap onto multiple lines
questions.explanation: `wrap` enables items to flow onto additional rows/columns when space runs out.

questions.question: `flex-flow` is a shorthand for which two properties?
questions.explanation: `flex-flow` combines `flex-direction` and `flex-wrap`.

questions.question: Which value of `justify-content` places the first item at the start, the last at the end, and distributes remaining space evenly between them?
questions.explanation: `space-between` gives no space at ends, equal space between items.

questions.question: `align-items: center;` will vertically centre items when the flex direction is:
questions.explanation: In `row`/`row-reverse`, cross axis is vertical; so `align-items: center;` centres them vertically.

questions.question: What does `align-content` control?
options: Alignment of individual items on cross axis
Distribution of space between flex lines when wrapping
questions.explanation: `align-content` works only with multiple lines, distributing space between them along the cross axis.

questions.question: The property that allows a flex item to override the container's `align-items` is ______.
questions.explanation: `align-self` sets cross-axis alignment for an individual item.

questions.question: What does `order: -1;` do to a flex item?
options: Moves it to the beginning of the visual order
questions.explanation: Lower `order` values appear earlier; -1 is before default 0.

questions.question: If all items have `flex-grow: 1;`, what happens to extra space?
questions.explanation: Equal `flex-grow` values divide the free space equally among items.

questions.question: What is the default value of `flex-shrink`?
questions.explanation: Default `flex-shrink` is 1, allowing items to shrink if needed.

questions.question: `flex-basis: auto;` means the initial size is based on:
options: The item's width/height property or content size
questions.explanation: `auto` looks at the item's explicit `width`/`height` or its content‑based size.

questions.question: What does `flex: 1;` expand to?
questions.explanation: `flex: 1;` sets grow=1, shrink=1, basis=0%.

questions.question: Which `flex` value makes an item inflexible, staying at its natural size?
questions.explanation: `flex: none` is `0 0 auto`; no grow, no shrink, auto basis.

questions.question: To create equal‑width columns regardless of content, you should use:
questions.explanation: `flex: 1;` (basis 0%) starts from zero, so columns share space equally.

questions.question: `flex: auto;` and `flex: 1;` always produce the same result.
questions.explanation: `flex: auto;` uses `flex-basis: auto`, meaning items start at their content size, so they may not be equal.

questions.question: How do you achieve a sticky footer layout with Flexbox?
options: Make the body a flex column container, give `main` `flex: 1;`
questions.explanation: The body as a flex column with `min-height: 100vh` and `main { flex: 1; }` pushes footer to bottom.

questions.question: Which property sets spacing between flex items without affecting outer edges?
questions.explanation: `gap` (row-gap, column-gap) controls gutters between flex items.

questions.question: If a flex container has `flex-direction: column;` and `justify-content: center;`, where will items be placed?
questions.explanation: In column layout, main axis is vertical; `justify-content` centres them vertically.

questions.question: `align-items: baseline;` aligns items by:
options: The baseline of their text content
questions.explanation: Baseline alignment ensures text sits on the same line even if font sizes differ.

questions.question: What is the default value of `align-items`?
questions.explanation: `align-items` defaults to `stretch`, making items fill the cross axis.

questions.question: To prevent an image from shrinking in a flex row, you set:
questions.explanation: `flex-shrink: 0;` keeps the image at its natural size.

questions.question: `display: flex;` makes the container a block‑level element, while `display: inline-flex;` makes it inline‑level.
questions.explanation: Both create flex containers; `flex` is block, `inline-flex` is inline.

questions.question: Which property would you use to vertically align a single item differently from its siblings?
questions.explanation: `align-self` overrides the container's `align-items` for that item.

questions.question: In a navigation bar with `justify-content: space-between;`, what happens if you have only one flex item?
options: It stretches to fill the container
questions.explanation: `space-between` aligns a single item to the start because there's no 'between' space to distribute.
